title: The month onion prices jumped across India
summary: In July 2013, the median onion market moved +67.0% in a month, 5.4 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 5.4σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for onion, across 470 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: July 2013
scenes.caption: Onion prices across 470 markets that reported in both June 2013 and July 2013.

scenes.headline: Median move +67.0%
scenes.caption: The typical market's onion price jumped 67.0% in one month. 97% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 5.4× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 5.4 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Punjab
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 76 reporting markets in Punjab had a median change of +93.4%.

scenes.headline: Panipat
scenes.caption: Panipat (Haryana), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹800 → ₹1,600 per quintal (+100.0%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
